question: How did the drain of wealth theory, as proposed by Dadabhai Naoroji, explain India’s poverty under British rule? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Decline of traditional industries
Export of Indian resources and wealth to Britain without fair compensation
Excessive population growth in India
Lack of agricultural development
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Export of Indian resources and wealth to Britain without fair compensation

Explanation:
Dadabhai Naoroji, through his 'Drain of Wealth' theory, explained that India's poverty under British rule was due to the continuous and unjust transfer of wealth from India to Britain. According to Naoroji, Britain exported Indian resources, raw materials, and goods without providing fair compensation, leading to the impoverishment of India. British policies deliberately deindustrialized India, turning it into a supplier of raw materials and a market for British manufactured goods. Naoroji detailed this theory in his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901). The drain included salaries of British officials, home charges, and profits of British companies. This theory became the economic foundation of the Indian national movement.

question_hi: दादाभाई नौरोजी द्वारा प्रस्तावित धन की निकासी सिद्धांत ने ब्रिटिश शासन के अधीन भारत की गरीबी को कैसे समझाया? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 1)

Explanation:
दादाभाई नौरोजी ने अपने सिद्धांत 'धन की निकासी' के माध्यम से बताया कि ब्रिटिश शासन के दौरान भारत का धन अनुचित तरीके से ब्रिटेन स्थानांतरित किया गया, जिससे भारत गरीब हुआ। नौरोजी के अनुसार, ब्रिटेन ने भारत से कच्चे माल और संसाधनों का निर्यात किया, लेकिन उचित मुआवजा नहीं दिया। इसके अलावा, ब्रिटिश नीतियों ने भारतीय उद्योगों को नष्ट किया और भारत को कच्चे माल के आपूर्तिकर्ता और ब्रिटिश वस्तुओं के बाजार में बदल दिया। नौरोजी ने अपनी पुस्तक 'पॉवर्टी एंड अन-ब्रिटिश रूल इन इंडिया' में इस सिद्धांत को विस्तार से समझाया। यह सिद्धांत भारतीय राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन का आर्थिक आधार बना।

question: Which of the following leaders of the Revolt of 1857 was the adopted son of Bajirao Peshwa II? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Nana Saheb
Raja Pratap Singh
Kunwar Singh
Tantiya Tope
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Nana Saheb

Explanation:
Among the leaders of the 1857 Revolt, Nana Saheb was the adopted son of Bajirao Peshwa II. Bajirao Peshwa II was exiled to Bithoor by the British and his pension was discontinued. Nana Saheb opposed this and became the leader of the revolt in Kanpur. He fought against the British and temporarily captured Kanpur. Tantiya Tope was his commander. Raja Pratap Singh led the revolt in Agra, and Kunwar Singh belonged to the Babu family of Bihar. Nana Saheb's original name was Dhondu Pant.

question: What was the policy of the 'Doctrine of Lapse' that caused discontent among Indian rulers before the rebellion of 1857? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: The British would pay subsidies to Indian rulers.
The British could annex a princely state if the ruler did not have a natural/biological heir.
The British would intervene in Indian courts.
The British government would adopt Indian rulers without heirs.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The British could annex a princely state if the ruler did not have a natural/biological heir.

Explanation:
The 'Doctrine of Lapse', implemented during Lord Dalhousie's tenure (1848-1856), allowed the British to annex any princely state whose ruler died without a natural male heir. This policy denied the traditional right of adopted sons to inherit the throne. Major states like Satara (1848), Nagpur (1854), Jhansi (1854), and Awadh (1856) were annexed under this policy. It caused widespread discontent among Indian rulers, becoming a key factor in the 1857 Rebellion. The doctrine was seen as a direct violation of Indian customs and a tool for British expansionism.

☛ Under what pretext was Awadh annexed? → Alleged misgovernment
question_hi: 1857 के विद्रोह से पहले भारतीय शासकों में असंतोष का कारण बनी 'डॉक्ट्रिन ऑफ़ लैप्स' की नीति क्या थी? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 2)

लॉर्ड डलहौजी के कार्यकाल (1848-1856) में लागू की गई 'व्यपगत सिद्धांत' (डॉक्ट्रिन ऑफ लैप्स) नीति के तहत, यदि किसी रियासत के शासक का कोई प्राकृतिक पुत्र उत्तराधिकारी नहीं होता, तो वह रियासत ब्रिटिश साम्राज्य में विलीन कर ली जाती थी। इस नीति ने गोद लिए पुत्रों के उत्तराधिकार के पारंपरिक अधिकार को नकार दिया। इससे कई प्रमुख रियासतें जैसे सतारा (1848), नागपुर (1854), झांसी (1854), और अवध (1856) अंग्रेजों के कब्जे में चली गईं। इस नीति ने भारतीय शासकों में गहरा असंतोष पैदा किया, जो 1857 के विद्रोह के प्रमुख कारणों में से एक बना।

question: Which day was marked by Mahatma Gandhi as the day of 'humiliation and prayer'? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: 6 April 1919
10 February 1919
23 March 1919
20 October 1919
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 6 April 1919

Explanation:
Mahatma Gandhi marked 6 April 1919 as the day of 'humiliation and prayer'. This day was observed in protest against the Rowlatt Act, passed by the British government, which allowed arrest of any person without trial. Gandhi considered it an attack on civil liberties and called for a nationwide hartal (strike) and prayer meetings. The term 'humiliation' referred to the insult to Indian rights by British rule, and 'prayer' signified Gandhi's non-violent resistance through prayer and fasting. The protest marked the beginning of the Rowlatt Satyagraha, a key phase in India's freedom struggle.

question: Who among the following was the leader of the 1857 Revolt from Kullu? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Ujjwal Shahi

Maulvi Liaqat Ali
Raja Pratap Singh
solution:

Explanation:

During the Revolt of 1857, discontent spread in the Kullu region as well, and Raja Pratap Singh took the lead. Under his leadership, soldiers from Kullu fought against the British. Raja Pratap Singh's contribution is considered significant in the history of Kullu.

question: Which of the following territories was annexed by the British Governor General Lord Dalhousie before the 1857 revolt that fueled the First War of Independence?  (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Awadh
Gwalior
Punjab
Assam
solution:

Explanation:
Lord Dalhousie annexed Awadh in 1856 under the pretext of 'misgovernment', though it was not under the 'Doctrine of Lapse'. The Nawab of Awadh, Wajid Ali Shah, was deposed and exiled. This annexation deeply angered the local nobility, landlords, and soldiers. A large number of soldiers in the Bengal Army were from Awadh, and the annexation directly fueled the 1857 revolt. Dalhousie also annexed other states like Punjab, Assam, and Gwalior during his tenure, but Awadh's annexation was the most significant in causing the rebellion. The annexation of Awadh is considered a major immediate cause of the First War of Independence, as it united various sections of Indian society against British rule.

question: Mirza Wajid Ali Shah was the king of which of the following regions during the Indian Rebellion of 1857? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 3)

Explanation:
During the Indian Rebellion of 1857, Mirza Wajid Ali Shah was the king of Awadh. Awadh was annexed by the British in 1856 under Lord Dalhousie's 'Doctrine of Lapse', and Wajid Ali Shah was exiled to Calcutta. Wajid Ali Shah was a patron of arts and music; he developed the dance form 'Parikhana'. question: The power to rule in India was transferred from the British East India Company to the British Parliament in which of the following years? (RPF Constable 2024 (07/03/2025) Shift 3)

question: Where did the sepoys go after their mutiny in Meerut? (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 2)

Bareilly
Kanpur
solution:

Explanation:
The revolt of 1857 began in the Meerut cantonment on 10 May 1857. The sepoys revolted against the use of greased cartridges by the British. After the mutiny, the sepoys marched overnight from Meerut to Delhi. They reached Delhi on 11 May 1857 and went to the Red Fort to meet the Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar. They proclaimed him as the Emperor of India and asked him to lead the revolt. Thus, Delhi became the epicenter of the revolt. While uprisings also occurred in Lucknow, Bareilly, and Kanpur, the Meerut sepoys directly proceeded to Delhi.

question: General Service Enlistment Act was passed in which of the following years? (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 3)

1856 AD

Explanation:
The General Service Enlistment Act was passed in 1856 AD. This act forced Indian soldiers to serve overseas if needed, which was against their religious beliefs as crossing the sea was considered a threat to their caste and religion. It was passed during the tenure of Lord Canning, the Governor-General of India. The Act was one of the major causes of the Indian Rebellion of 1857. Indian soldiers had never been required to serve abroad before, and this act created widespread resentment among them, as it interfered with their traditional practices and led to a feeling of betrayal. The Act, combined with other grievances like the Enfield rifle cartridge issue, sparked the rebellion.

question: Under the British Colonial rule, what accounted for most of India’s exports by the 1850s? (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Manufactured goods
Raw materials like raw cotton, opium and indigo
Processed goods like fine cotton and silk
Spices and tea
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Raw materials like raw cotton, opium and indigo

Explanation:
Under British colonial rule, by the 1850s, most of India's exports consisted of raw materials like raw cotton, opium, and indigo. Britain needed cheap raw materials for its Industrial Revolution. India's traditional handicraft and textile industries were deliberately destroyed, and India became a supplier of raw materials and a market for British manufactured goods. The export of raw cotton fed British textile mills, opium was smuggled into China to balance trade, and indigo was used as a dye. This policy led to a trade surplus for India but drained its wealth and stunted industrial growth.

☛ Indigo export importance → Dye for British textile industry
☛ Impact of raw material exports → Deindustrialization and economic exploitation of India

question: The British police attacked Lala Lajpat Rai during a peaceful demonstration against the _______ in 1928. (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Hindu casteism
Simon Commission
unjust taxes during famine
British salt monopoly
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Simon Commission

Explanation:
In 1928, the British government sent the Simon Commission to India, which had no Indian members. This sparked widespread protests across the country. On October 30, 1928, a peaceful demonstration was led by Lala Lajpat Rai in Lahore against the Commission. The police, under the orders of Superintendent James Scott, charged with batons, severely injuring Lala Lajpat Rai. He succumbed to his injuries on November 17, 1928. The incident galvanized the Indian freedom movement and led to revenge by Bhagat Singh, who killed police officer John Saunders.

question: Which of the following was the most significant development after the revolt of 1857? (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 3)
options:
Indian people formed associations, societies, and organisations which led to the
formation of Indian National Congress.
Indian people dropped the idea of liberating themselves.
Indian people formed close relationship with the British empire.
Indians started reorganising themselves for another armed revolt.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Indian people formed associations, societies, and organisations which led to the formation of Indian National Congress.

Explanation:
After the failure of the 1857 revolt, Indians realized that armed struggle against the British was not feasible. This led to the rise of a new political consciousness, where educated Indians began to voice their demands through constitutional and peaceful means. Consequently, in 1885, the Indian National Congress was formed, which became a major platform for the Indian freedom movement. The other options are incorrect because Indians did not abandon the idea of liberation, nor did they form close ties with the British empire; instead, they reorganised politically. The formation of the Congress was a significant development that channeled nationalist sentiments into organised political action.

question:
Which of the following statements accurately describes the land revenue systems
implemented by the British in India and their impact on agriculture? (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: The Zamindari system, covering the majority of land, provided incentives for cultivators to invest in their farms.

The Zamindari system focused on high revenue collection by zamindars, leaving
cultivators with little to reinvest in agriculture.
In the Mahalwari system, land was held by individual cultivators who had autonomy over their land management.
The Ryotwari and Mahalwari systems covered 4% and 38% of the land, respectively, and provided some development for improving land fertility.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Zamindari system focused on high revenue collection by zamindars, leaving cultivators with little to reinvest in agriculture.

Explanation:
During British rule, three major land revenue systems were implemented: Zamindari (1793), Ryotwari (1820), and Mahalwari (1822). In the Zamindari system, zamindars were granted revenue collection rights, but they often extracted excessive taxes from peasants. This left cultivators with little surplus to reinvest in agriculture, leading to stagnation in productivity and high indebtedness. The Ryotwari system taxed individual cultivators directly, while Mahalwari made the village collectively responsible. Both systems introduced some improvements like irrigation, but the tax burden remained heavy. The Zamindari system, covering about 57% of British India, particularly discouraged investment as zamindars had no incentive to improve land they did not own, worsening rural poverty.

☛ Role of zamindars → Revenue collectors, not landowners
☛ Regions under Ryotwari system → Madras, Bombay, Assam
☛ Revenue unit in Mahalwari system → Village (mahal)
☛ Worst impact of land revenue systems → Lack of agricultural capital and decline in output

question: On hearing about which of the following on 4 February 1922, did Mahatma Gandhi go on a five-day fast and suspend the Non-cooperation Movement? (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Kakori conspiracy
Chauri Chaura Incident
Noakhali riots
Jallianwala Bagh massacre
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chauri Chaura Incident

Explanation:
On 4 February 1922, a violent clash occurred between peasants and police at Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur district, Uttar Pradesh. 22 policemen were burnt alive. Deeply distressed by this violence, Mahatma Gandhi immediately suspended the Non-cooperation Movement. He believed the movement had deviated from the principle of non-violence. He also observed a 5-day fast as penance. This suspension led to disappointment among many leaders, which later resulted in the formation of the Swaraj Party. The Chauri Chaura Incident is a pivotal turning point in India's freedom struggle.

4 फरवरी 1922 को उत्तर प्रदेश के गोरखपुर जिले के चौरी-चौरा में किसानों और पुलिस के बीच हिंसक झड़प हुई। इसमें 22 पुलिसकर्मी जिंदा जल गए। इस घटना से दुखी होकर महात्मा गांधी ने असहयोग आंदोलन को तुरंत स्थगित कर दिया। गांधीजी का मानना था कि आंदोलन अहिंसा के सिद्धांत से भटक गया है। उन्होंने 5 दिन का उपवास भी किया। इस स्थगन से कई नेताओं में निराशा फैली, जिसके कारण बाद में स्वराज पार्टी का गठन हुआ। चौरी-चौरा कांड भारतीय स्वतंत्रता संग्राम की एक महत्वपूर्ण मोड़ है।

question:
In addition to Awadh, which of the following were the other territories annexed by the
British under various pretexts? (RPF Constable 2024 (09/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Assam and Nagaland
Mysore and Hyderabad
Bengal and Punjab
Jhansi and Satara
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Jhansi and Satara

Explanation:
The British used the 'Doctrine of Lapse' to expand their empire in India. Under this policy, if a princely state's ruler had no son, the state would be annexed by the British Empire. Lord Dalhousie implemented this doctrine most vigorously. Jhansi and Satara were prominent territories annexed by the British under this policy. Jhansi was annexed in 1853, and Satara in 1848. Awadh was annexed in 1856 under the pretext of 'misgovernment'. Assam and Nagaland were annexed through other processes. Mysore and Hyderabad came under British control through the subsidiary alliance system.

question: What was the time period of the Sayyid dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: 1414–1451
1414–1446
1424–1445
1414–1430
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1414–1451

Explanation:
The Sayyid dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate was founded by Khizr Khan in 1414 CE after the decline of the Tughlaq dynasty. The last ruler of this dynasty was Alam Shah, who ruled until 1451 CE, after which the Lodhi dynasty came to power. The Sayyids predominantly ruled over Delhi and its surrounding regions. During this period, the sultanate's military strength weakened, and regional kingdoms gained influence. The Sayyid dynasty ruled for a total of 37 years.

question_hi: दिल्ली सल्तनत के सैय्यद वंश का समय काल क्या था? (RPF Constable 2024 (10/03/2025) Shift 1)

1424-1445
1414-1430
solution_hi:

Explanation:
